findings.title: Source staging writes through a dangling final target symlink
findings.requirement: The source-staging helper must reject every symlink component and confine staged copies to the isolated worktree.

evidence.observation: The committed method states that source staging rejects every symlink component, verifies each file by SHA-256, and leaves tracked repository files unchanged.

target_path rejects a target component only when current.exists() and current.is_symlink() are both true. For a dangling final symlink, exists() follows the missing referent and returns false while is_symlink() is true, so the symlink bypasses this gate.

Write mode repeats the exists()-before-is_symlink() guard and then calls shutil.copy2(source, target). copy2 follows the dangling destination symlink, creates its referent outside the worktree, hashes through that alias, and reports success.

observations: The bounded fixture placed docs/rulebooks/rulebook.pdf as a symlink to a nonexistent file outside the synthetic target root; before staging, is_symlink() was true, exists() was false, and the external referent did not exist.
The public stager main returned 0, retained the symlink, created the external referent, copied the exact source bytes through the symlink, and reported successful staging.
The same probe confirmed that an existing intermediate target symlink is rejected, isolating the bypass to dangling target components hidden by exists().

findings.impact: A pre-existing dangling target symlink can redirect a nominally worktree-confined source copy to create a file outside the worktree while the helper returns success and verifies the bytes through the alias. This violates the documented every-component and containment guarantees and makes the reported worktree staging result unreliable.
findings.recommendedFix: Reject current.is_symlink() unconditionally in target_path, before any exists() test, and reject target.is_symlink() before the write-mode regular-file guard. Prefer a dirfd/O_NOFOLLOW-based destination open to bind the check to the copy. Add a public-main regression with a dangling final target symlink and assert both nonzero exit and absence of the external referent.

details: Canonical write and --check positive controls returned 0.
Empty, backslash, leading-dot, dot, dotdot, duplicate-separator, trailing-separator, absolute-in-repository, and sibling-prefix output aliases were rejected.

Each of the eight output components from docs through the final filename was replaced in turn by an in-root symlink; write and --check mode rejected all sixteen cases before any rejected-case filesystem change.
The public stager rejected a raw --source-root symlink and a symlink in an ancestor of the raw source-root path.
The public stager rejected source-prefix symlinks at docs, docs/rulebooks, assets, assets/tts-mod, and assets/tts-mod/extract, plus descendant directory and source-file symlinks.
A source-relative filename containing a literal backslash was rejected as noncanonical.
Canonical synthetic stage/check controls returned 0, and the real isolated-worktree --check verified 1,098 files with zero copies.

testsRun.result: 1,098 files current/checked; zero copies and zero copied bytes
PATH-002 and requested PATH-003 controls passed; dangling final target-symlink write-through reproduced
exact candidate worktree remained clean with no tracked repository modifications

issuesEncountered: The first custom-probe run incorrectly required zero target writes before an assets-prefix source symlink was reached, even though the helper processes the valid docs tree first. That probe-only assertion was corrected; the complete probe reran from fresh temporary roots and exited 0. No failed probe output was used as candidate evidence.
